top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) is the achievement I can defend most fully: the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct step from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, 1e-18 performance has been confirmed independently by several laboratories through clock-to-clock comparisons, the allocation of two names is clean and widely shared, and the consequences (geodesy, constants tests, dark-matter searches) are measurable. The citation should name the lattice and magic wavelength, not records or the redefinition of the second. P002 is second because IceCube is a real observational discovery, but a one-name credit for a large collaboration is not one I can defend. P003 is scientifically strong but its three-name allocation among five credited names is contested; any award is preferred to none.
recusal_note: No direct conflict apparent from profile; as an astroparticle experimentalist in PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur I have no stated tie to the laureates in any proposal, though IceCube (P002) is in my own field and I would lean on outside experts for credit.
